turns.content: Let an admissible family contain k triples (a_i,b_i,c_i) of nonnegative integers, each summing to n, with every coordinate separately pairwise distinct across triples. What is the sum of all 3k coordinates?
What is the smallest possible sum of k distinct nonnegative integers?
Use the stars-and-bars count of all nonnegative solutions to a+b+c=n as the sole method for the sharp admissible-family maximum.
For n=3m, construct an explicit family that attains the upper bound and prove that its triples satisfy the distinct-coordinate conditions.
Count the triples in that construction and compare the count with the upper bound.
Adapt the construction to n congruent to 1 and 2 modulo 3, checking the distinct-coordinate conditions in each case.
Combine the upper bound and constructions to determine N(n) for every n>=2.
